newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yemen, Eritrea sign Red Sea arbitration pact.
newsitem.headline: Yemen, Eritrea sign Red Sea arbitration pact.

text.p: Yemen and Eritrea signed an accord in Paris on Thursday to set up a court to resolve their territorial dispute over Red Sea islands on busy oil tanker routes.
The French Foreign Ministry, which mediated the deal, said the accord would lead to creation of a five-judge arbitration court in London that would start work by April 11, 1997.

The pact was signed at the foreign ministry by Eritrea's Minister for Marine Resources Saleh Meki and by Hussein Ali Al-Hubaishi, a legal advisor to the Yemeni government, the ministry said in a statement.

Arab Yemen and African Eritrea, facing each other across the Red Sea, both claim sovereignty over the small, arid Hanish islands. The dispute led to clashes in which at least 12 people died last December.

"The court will have to give two rulings, the first on the question of territorial sovereignty and of the zone disputed by the two sides, the second fixing maritime frontiers," the ministry said in a statement. "This will take several months."

Each country will appoint two judges to the court and the four judges in turn will name a fifth presiding judge. The head of the International Court of Justice in the Hague will name the presiding judge if they fail to reach accord by the end of 1996.
The two sides both agreed to site the court in London.

The two countries asked the United Nations to mediate after last year's clashes, and U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali turned the negotiating process over to France. Egypt and Ethiopia had also exerted mediation efforts.
The islands are near vital shipping lanes used by more than 100 ships daily on a route where tankers carry 125,000 barrels of oil a day from the Gulf to customers in Europe via Egypt's Suez Canal.

The conflict worsened last August when Yemen threatened to take military action if mediation failed to defuse a crisis triggered by dispatch of Eritrean troops to Lesser Hanish island. Eritrea later said it had withdrawn its forces.
